coverage.remaining: None. The whole document was read, narrative, figure captions, footnotes and the evaluation guidelines.
coverage.note: A 133-page thematic statement with no inventory table, no APNs and no survey results, and still one of the denser documents in the register: 139 distinct numbered-address strings, of which about 100 are real addresses. Three things shape the read. First, the statement marks nearly every address it prints as (extant) or (demolished), which is the most useful convention any document in this register has used — 18 addresses are marked demolished and are recorded here as rejected rather than resolved, because the building the fact belongs to is gone even where the number still resolves to a parcel. Second, its footnotes are numbered and rendered inline by pdftotext, so a footnote marker abutting a street name produces phantom addresses: 164 Haight, 195 Haight, 405 Haight, 200 Scott and 264 Scott are all footnote numbers, not buildings, and every candidate was checked against the character before it. Third, the real addresses are spread evenly through the narrative, the figure captions, the footnotes and the evaluation guidelines, and the guidelines section at the back repeats and sometimes corrects addresses given earlier — the Avalon is 1268 Sutter in the narrative and 1244-68 Sutter in the guidelines. The document contradicts itself three times and each is recorded on the findings: the Fillmore Auditorium is 1805 Geary three times and 1806 Geary once; California Hall is 600 Turk in the narrative and 625 Polk in the landmark list, the two street frontages of one corner building; and a clothing and herbal business is at 1031 Stanyan in one chapter and 1301 Stanyan in another. One address was deliberately not extracted: the only thing the statement says about 1703 Buchanan Street concerns a named individual's private sexual life, which the privacy limits in the root AGENTS.md bar. Two addresses are outside San Francisco (La Honda and Berkeley) and are rejected as out of scope.
